q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of ACSR conductor?
title: ACSR conductor carbon footprint per tonne
short: ACSR is aluminium wire stranded around a galvanised steel core. Split the conductor's weight into aluminium and steel, multiply each by its supplier's figure, then add wire drawing and stranding energy per tonne of conductor.
audience: Conductor makers supplying transmission and distribution utilities

ul: Aluminium rod, which carries most of the footprint.
Grease and wooden or steel drums.
Stranding aluminium layers over the steel core.

p: Report per tonne or per km by conductor code, since the aluminium to steel ratio differs between sizes. Primary aluminium smelted on coal power carries a high figure, so ask for the rod supplier's own number.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per tonne (one month)
lines: Plant total: 85,200 / 800 = 106.5 kg CO2 per tonne
Add aluminium rod and steel core wire for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
